title: Limits, when to stop, and the pre-trade checklist

inOneLine.simple: Your plan also says how much you can lose in a day, how many trades you take, and when you stop. A [[pre-trade-checklist]] checks each trade against it.
inOneLine.balanced: A daily loss limit and a maximum trade count cap the damage from a bad day or a bad mood. The pre-trade checklist asks five questions before every trade: in my plan? stop set? risk within limit? important news due soon? calm, and not trying to win back a loss?

explain.simple: Even good rules lose sometimes. Bad days happen. Your plan should say when to stop. A daily loss limit stops you after you lose a set amount. A maximum number of trades stops you from trading too much. Add plain stop rules too, such as "stop if I feel angry" or "stop before a big news release". Then, before each trade, the app shows a short checklist. Is this trade in my plan? Is a stop loss set? Is the risk within my limit? Is there important news due soon for this market? Am I calm, and not trying to win back a loss? If an answer raises a caution (for example no stop, risk over your limit, news due soon, not calm, or not sure), wait or skip that trade. The app lists the cautions; the decision to wait is yours.
explain.balanced: Limits work best as numbers you can check, not feelings. Write them as an amount of money or a count of trades. The pre-trade checklist sits before you go to MetaTrader or place a paper trade. It is short on purpose, so you use it every time. When you want to change a limit, do it after the session, save a new plan version, and note why. Then you can compare versions in your journal instead of drifting without noticing.

assumptions: Example risk per trade: 1% = 20 USD (example only)
Losses equal the planned risk (no slippage)
steps: Trade 1: stop hit, −20 USD. Day total −20 USD.
Trade 2: target hit, +40 USD. Day total +20 USD.
Trade 3: stop hit, −20 USD. Day total 0 USD.
Trade 4: stop hit, −20 USD. Day total −20 USD. That is 4 trades, the maximum, so the learner stops for the day even though the loss limit was not reached.

assumptions: Fictional paper trade idea on GBP/USD
A major news release is due in 15 minutes
The learner's plan says: no new trades from 30 minutes before major news
steps: In my plan? Yes, the setup matches the entry rule.
Important news due soon? Yes, within 30 minutes. That raises a caution, and the plan says no new trades now.
One caution is enough. The learner skips the trade and writes down why.

explainSimpler: Limits are the brakes. The checklist is checking the mirrors before you pull out.
commonMistake: Raising the daily loss limit in the middle of a losing day "just this once". That turns the limit into a suggestion.

quickCheck.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the five pre-trade checklist questions?

options.explanation: No: this is one of the five questions.
Right: nobody can know that. The checklist checks your process, not the outcome.

options.text: Am I calm, and not trying to win back a loss?
options.explanation: No: this is one of the five questions.

quickCheck.prompt: The setup is in your plan, the stop is set, risk is within your limit and you are calm. A major release is due in 10 minutes, and your plan says no new trades within 30 minutes of major news. What do you do?

options.text: Take it: four out of five is good enough
options.explanation: No: the checklist is not a score. One answer that raises a caution means you wait or skip that trade.
Right: the news rule says no, so you wait.

quickCheck.prompt: When is the right time to change your daily loss limit?

options.text: After the session, saved as a new plan version
options.explanation: Right: calm changes, recorded, so you can compare versions.

options.text: When you hit it and want one more trade
options.explanation: No: that is exactly when the limit is meant to stop you.

doItNow.instructions: In More → Tools → Trading plan, set your risk per trade, daily loss limit, maximum trades per day, and your "when to stop" rules. Save the plan. Then open the pre-trade checklist and run it on one paper trade idea, even if you do not take the trade.

homework: Read your saved plan out loud. It should fit on one page. Anything you would not follow on a bad day, simplify.
